title: StoredEvent domain schema version and projection commit seam
description: Objective: give StoredEvent a domain schema version for later upcasters to dispatch on, and expose a commit seam that runs a caller-supplied apply inside the existing event transaction. Task B of a 2-way split of task-50874e67. Deliverable: a domainSchemaVersion field threaded through write and read paths, a PROJECTION_APPLY_FAILED code added to the closed DurableStoreErrorCode union, and a seam on the event transaction gated on COMMITTED disposition with the wrap at the invocation site. File map established during blocking analysis, use it rather than rediscovering: commit() body is in event-ledger-transaction.ts (event-ledger.ts is a facade needing no edit); STORED_EVENT_SELECT_COLUMNS is in read-page-queries.ts; the sole INSERT site is event-ledger-append.ts; sqlite-event-store.ts must thread seam options through its fixed one-arg commit over private #core. NOT in scope: the schema tables and migration (Task A), the projection fold, relay, or subscriptions. Hard dependencies: SQLite schema v3 projection tables and migration (Task A) — the columns must exist first. Owned paths: packages/store/src/store-contracts.ts, store-input*.ts, event-ledger-append*.ts, event-ledger-transaction*.ts, event-read-decode*.ts, read-page-queries.ts, sqlite-event-store.ts, one new seam test, and the event-read-model-contract.test.ts key-set edit. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: StoredEvent carries a domain schema version written on append and read back unchanged through every read path, sufficient for a later upcaster to dispatch on without guessing.

The event transaction exposes a commit seam that runs a caller-supplied apply inside the same transaction as the append, gated on COMMITTED disposition, proven by a test where a failing apply rolls the event back with PROJECTION_APPLY_FAILED.
PROJECTION_APPLY_FAILED is added to the closed DurableStoreErrorCode union and maps to truth and retryability like every other member; the union stays closed.

Existing tests pass with ONLY the forced key-set update in event-read-model-contract.test.ts, whose toStrictEqual pins the exact StoredEvent key set. No test is weakened or skipped. The focused store typecheck and test command exits 0 with only owned paths committed.
taskRails: Task A must land first. The domainSchemaVersion column and projection tables have to exist before this threads through them.
Build the seam, not the feature. A projection fold, upcaster, relay, or subscription implemented here starves the downstream tasks and rebuilds the oversized task that was split.
A failed apply must roll back the event append. A partial write is never acceptable, no matter how green the tests are.
The one permitted test edit is the StoredEvent key set in event-read-model-contract.test.ts. Everything else passes unchanged.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only.

CORRECTION to the plan's stated mechanism for the EffectEventDraft Omit (the conclusion holds, the reason differs — recorded so step-6's red-team tests the right thing): identifyCommandEffects (store-digests.ts:190-221) hashes an EXPLICIT FIELD LIST, never key enumeration. So an extra runtime property riding the append-site spread cannot change digest bytes, and write/replay could not diverge that way. The Omit is load-bearing for TYPECHECK instead, and provably so: event-read-decode.ts:55-58 derives `DecodedReceiptEventBody = Omit<EffectEventDraft, ...>` and decodeReceiptEventBody :208-217 returns only 4 fields; event-read-materialization.ts:156-162 builds its replay effectEvent literal from that. If EffectEventDraft required domainSchemaVersion, BOTH would fail to compile. Step-6 will red-team the typecheck failure, not a phantom digest divergence.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — new packages/store/src/store-domain-schema-version.test.ts (<=250). Cases: (1) ROUNDTRIP: commit an EventDraft WITHOUT domainSchemaVersion -> read back via readEvents/readEventsAfter -> StoredEvent.domainSchemaVersion === 'moe-domain-schema/0' (the DDL default constant, now also a TS constant DOMAIN_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION); commit WITH an explicit caller value (e.g. 'moe-domain-schema/2') -> read back UNCHANGED through every read path (by-aggregate, by-position cursor) — DoD: written on append, read back unchanged, sufficient for a later upcaster to dispatch on; (2) VALIDATION: snapshotCommitInput rejects non-string/empty/oversized domainSchemaVersion with the store's stable input codes (bounded length — reuse requireIdentifier-style validation; caller values are opaque, NOT pinned to the constant — upcasters dispatch on recorded values); (3) DIGEST NEUTRALITY (the replay-corruption guard): effect digests must NOT include the field — commit events with a non-default value, then loadReceipt must succeed (replay rebuilds effect events WITHOUT the field; if it entered identifyCommandEffects the write/replay sides would diverge and every receipt would throw STORE_CORRUPT); requestSha256 unchanged (hashes only aggregateId/expectedVersion/commandBytes); (4) rejection-audit path: a decision rejection's audit event carries the DEFAULT constant (decision-ledger-canonical builds its event literal directly). Run focused test — RED.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED achieved. New packages/store/src/store-domain-schema-version.test.ts (208 lines, under the 250 cap), 13 cases: 10 FAIL / 3 pass, exit 1.

Failures are all for the correct reason — `expected undefined to be 'moe-domain-schema/0'` (field absent) and the 6 validation cases where commit currently SUCCEEDS instead of throwing.

Coverage vs plan:
(1) ROUNDTRIP default + explicit, each asserted through ALL THREE StoredEvent read paths via a readEveryPath() helper — readEvents, readAggregateEvents (by-aggregate cursor), readEventsAfter (by-position cursor).
(1b) Added beyond plan, cheap and directly serves the DoD's "sufficient for a later upcaster to dispatch on": one commit carrying THREE events with different versions (explicit, other explicit, omitted-defaulting) asserts per-event resolution, not per-commit.
(2) VALIDATION table-driven, 6 cases: empty, number, null, object, 513-char oversize, embedded NUL. Each asserts STORE_INPUT_INVALID, the exact message `events[0].domainSchemaVersion must be well-formed, non-empty, at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, and contain no NUL`, AND that nothing persisted (empty ledger + aggregate version 0) — a rejected commit must not half-write.
(3) DIGEST NEUTRALITY, two angles: (a) two fresh stores committing byte-identical input differing ONLY in domainSchemaVersion must produce identical requestSha256 AND effectSha256; (b) getCommandReceipt on a non-default-version commit must re-prove the stored digest (verified path: event-read-model.ts:28-32 -> loadReceipt -> event-read-materialization.ts:197 recompute + STORE_CORRUPT on mismatch).
(4) Rejection-audit event carries the default constant, plus a decision's committed business events carry an explicit caller value (covers decision-ledger-canonical's direct literal AND the decision commit path).

Two mechanical notes for the next step:
- A literal NUL byte got into the source on first write and Edit could not match it (Read renders it as a space). Replaced via serena regex with `String.fromCharCode(0)`; `grep -nP '\x00'` now reports no raw NUL bytes in the file. Do not hand-type control characters into source.
- proposedDecision() from command-decision-test-helpers is hard-scoped to projectId "project-1", so the two decision cases pass an explicit projectId through withStore or they die on PROJECT_SCOPE_MISMATCH, not on the assertion under test.

Zero production files touched in this step.
